predecessors.name: Shang dynasty
predecessors.text: the old Shang heartland round Zhaoge: after the Duke of Zhou defeated the rebellion, 'Kang Shu, a younger brother of King Wu of Zhou was given a fief centred on Zhaoge'

successors.name: Qin dynasty
successors.text: Yewang, where Wey's ruler was relocated in 241 and where the state survived 'nominally as a Qin vassal with no real independence'; Qin Er Shi deposed Lord Jiao in 209

ledger.x: c. 1040: the Zhou enfeoff Kang Shu at Zhaoge and Wey begins on the old Shang heartland north of the Yellow River. 'Kang Shu, a younger brother of King Wu of Zhou was given a fief centred on Zhaoge' after the Duke of Zhou defeated the rebellion; infobox 'Zhaoge: c. 1040-661 BCE'. The page gives the year as the…
659: Wey, restored after the Rong killed Duke Yi at Zhaoge in 660 with the help of Duke Huan of Qi, moves its capital to Chuqiu.
635: Wey wipes out the small state of Xing.
629: the capital moves to Diqiu, where it stays until 241.
550: Cliopatria passes one cell to Jin.
450: Cliopatria passes 9 cells (about 1,000 km2) to Jin.
404: Cliopatria passes one cell to Wei.
346: Wey's ruler is downgraded from duke to marquis, and by 320 to 'jun'.
By 320: Wey is reduced to the county of Puyang.
241: Qin captures Puyang and Wey's ruler flees to Yewang.
241: the capital moves from Diqiu to Yewang.
209: Qin Er Shi deposes Lord Jiao and Wey ends, the last of the Zhou fiefs to fall.

wars.name: Rong invasion of Wey
wars.outcome: The Rong attacked Zhaoge and killed Duke Yi; Wey was restored with the help of Duke Huan of Qi and moved to Chuqiu (659).

wars.name: Wey's destruction of Xing
wars.outcome: Xing wiped out in 635 (632 in the Spring and Autumn table); Jin and Wey are its listed successors.

wars.name: Qin's capture of Puyang
wars.outcome: Qin captured Puyang during its attack on Wei; Wey's ruler was relocated to Yewang as a nominal Qin vassal.

certainty.note: Wey is a small state on the Yellow River plain whose borders are known only by its capitals and by 'the county of Puyang'; no survey lines exist.
